bullets: Game 2 of 6 in a single-deck video (video time 226.2-518.2s); a win on the overtime damage lead over 'Yaco' on a Golden Knight log-bait deck (Wall Breakers, Skeletons, Dark Prince, Goblin Barrel, Rascals, Golden Knight, Princess, Evo Giant Snowball). No tower fell on either side: last readable state is own 2216 / 2579 HP against enemy 748 / 3748. 'Guys, we won. There's no way for them to get to our tower and we already have the Evo baby dragon for defense' (t=499-504). The in-game clock OCR failed for the whole video, so all timings are video seconds.

He calls this matchup one of the deck's hard ones on sight — 'This actually might be one of those difficult matchups that I was talking about here' (t=250-253) — for two named reasons: Evolution Giant Snowball answers the Evolution Royal Hogs (t=244-247), and back-line Princesses chip for free because logging them opens a Golden Knight plus Goblin Barrel chain onto his Skeletons (t=307-316).

The game plan is deliberate attrition, stated after conceding 1900 HP on the left at t=322-326: 'this is going to be a lot of damage, guys, but I think it was for the greater good... not to let him have control of the game. At least this way it should be kind of like a stalemate where I'm just constantly defending his pushes but I'll be able to do it really really well' (t=321-334).

Defensive core is Cannon in column 8-9 cycled roughly every 20 seconds (t=246, 286, 315, 344, 363, 400, 417, 438, 455, 493) with Skeletons plus Electro Spirit on top and the Mighty Miner parked at his own bridge; The Log is reserved for the Goblin Barrel and played on his own tower on read (t=264-268).

Royal Hogs are committed only three times in five minutes — split at t=337 and single-lane at t=367 for chip and evolution cycle ('I do need to start getting to the evo and this will be a little bit of chip damage', t=339-342), then twice into one lane in overtime for the kill.

The winning push (t=447-492) is built off a spell read: 'he doesn't have a big spell so I can try to stack up baby dragons if the moment presents itself' (t=439-443). Two Baby Dragons behind a Mighty Miner, with Evo Royal Hogs sent twice, take the enemy left tower 4097 -> 1038 HP with no answering damage — 'That was one of the biggest pushes I've ever made' (t=492-495).
Lightning is carried but never confirmed cast in this game; he twice talks himself out of using it on the Princesses because of the tempo it concedes (t=364-369, t=432-436).
Substitutions he offers for the list: Golden Knight, Knight or Valkyrie in place of the Mighty Miner (not Skeleton King), and Archer Queen in place of the Baby Dragon (t=276-301).

new_deck.rationale: A 3.4-elixir list whose only win condition is Royal Hogs, supported by four cards of 1-3 elixir (Skeletons, Electro Spirit, The Log, Cannon) that let it out-cycle and out-defend rather than build a push.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Royal Hogs are the only damage card; everything else is a cheap answer that comes back around fast — Skeletons, Electro Spirit, The Log and Cannon average two elixir and cover swarms, resets, barrels and ground tanks between them. Mighty Miner is the deck's swing piece rather than a second win condition: Ryley plays him almost exclusively on his own bridge tiles to block a lane and deny a Goblin Barrel behind a tank, and spends the 1-elixir Explosive Escape as an elixir trade — to keep a Cannon alive, to snipe a Princess, or to punish a barrel he baited with The Log ("mighty miner predict a goblin barrel cuz then we can pop off the ability", t=350-352). Baby Dragon is the only air unit and is cycled to its evolution on purpose, because two evolved Baby Dragons behind the Mighty Miner is the deck's actual kill push once the opponent's spell list is known to be small. The deck accepts chip damage in exchange for never losing tempo — "not to let him have control of the game... I'm just constantly defending his pushes" (t=323-334) — and converts in one overtime window rather than across the match. The obvious weaknesses in this game were a lack of any cheap answer to back-line Princess chip (Lightning is too expensive to justify) and Evolution Giant Snowball on the Royal Hogs.
